# ADR-002: Use a Deferred Service Provider

<!-- Generated by seed-golden-context | Last updated: 2026-05-11 -->

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Laravel service providers can be eager (always instantiated on bootstrap) or deferred (`$defer = true`), meaning the container binding is only resolved when the service is first requested.

The Contentful `Client` makes no HTTP calls on construction, but it is still an object that reads config and instantiates several internal components. Not every Laravel request will need the Contentful client (e.g., unauthenticated pages, queue workers for non-content jobs).

## Decision

`ContentfulServiceProvider` sets `$defer = true` and implements `provides()` returning `[Client::class]`. Laravel will not construct the provider or the client until something in the application resolves `Client::class` (or the `ContentfulDelivery` facade).

## Consequences

- Applications that never touch the Contentful client pay zero construction cost.
- The provider's `boot()` method (which publishes and merges config) still runs at boot time — this is standard Laravel behavior and required for `mergeConfigFrom` to work before any config reads happen.
- Developers expecting eager instantiation (e.g., for connection-check behavior at boot) will need to resolve the facade explicitly.
